issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires Farm.animals to be a List implemented using an ArrayList and instructs students to initialize an ArrayList and provide a getter/setter. The provided solution instead declares animals as a Queue and initializes it with a LinkedList. This contradicts the specification (List/ArrayList) and changes the public API (getter/setter types) that students are instructed to implement, which can confuse students and lead to mismatched implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement: change the Farm.animals declaration to use List<Animal> and initialize it with new ArrayList<>() in the no-argument constructor. Update the getter and setter signatures to use List<Animal> and adjust addAnimal/feedAllAnimals/singFarmSong implementations accordingly. Alternatively, if the intended design was to use a Queue, update the problem statement and UML to explicitly state Queue/LinkedList instead of List/ArrayList.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify the farm's animal collection as a List<Animal> and explicitly instruct initializing it as an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor, but the provided solution implements the collection as a Queue<Animal> backed by a LinkedList. This diverging type/name for the same conceptual entity (the farm's animals collection) can confuse students who are instructed to use List/ArrayList in the tasks but see Queue/LinkedList in the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the same collection type across artifacts. Update the solution (and template if necessary) to declare the animals attribute as List<Animal>, initialize it with new ArrayList<>(), and have the getter/setter use List<Animal>. This aligns the implementation with the problem statement and UML, reducing mapping confusion for students.
